newsitem.title: PERU: Peru president's popularity falls to 52 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru president's popularity falls to 52 pct - poll.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's public approval rating dipped to 52 percent at the end of October, from 55 percent at the beginning of the month, a leading pollster said Monday.
The survey of 400 Lima residents over the weekend by Peruvian polling firm Apoyo SA also showed that 41 percent disapproved of Fujimori's record.

Fujimori, who took office in 1990 and won re-election last year with an overwhelming 64 percent of the vote, has held relatively high popularity ratings during his term due mainly to the virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reforms and strong, personalized leadership style.

But the administration's failure to reduce high levels of poverty and unemployment, Fujimori's perceived authoritarianism, his possible bid for a third term, and the unpopularity of his security adviser Vladimiro Montesinos are starting to take a toll on the president's standing, analysts say.
The Apoyo poll, with a margin of error of five percent, also showed that 71 percent favored a referendum on whether Fujimori should be allowed to run for the presidency a third time in 2000.

Congress recently approved an interpretation of the constitution that would allow Fujimori to run for the presidency again in 2000, but opposition legislators are campaigning for a referendum on the issue.
